newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Valecom wins new partner for CVRD bid.
newsitem.headline: Valecom wins new partner for CVRD bid.

text.p: Brazilian metal and metallurgical group Caemi is signing an agreement Tuesday to join the Valecom consortium which will bid at the privatization auction of state mining giant CVRD, Valecom said in a statement.

The privatization of CVRD kicks off April 29 with the auction of a 40-45-percent voting stake in the company on the Rio de Janeiro stock exchange for a minimum price of 3 billion reais ($2.82 billion).

The Valecom consortium is being led by Brazilian metal, cement and pulp group Votorantim and South Africa's Anglo-American Corp which have equal stakes in the consortium amounting to more than 50 percent jointly.
A group of 12 Japanese steelmakers and trading companies led by Nippon Steel Corp and two Brazilian pension funds, Centrus and Sistel, have also joined Valecom.
The Japanese have a 10 percent stake in Valecom and the pension funds already have a joint voting stake in CVRD of 2.8 percent.

The consortium is also holding talks with other investors, including CVRD's employees who can acquire 4.45 percent of CVRD voting shares under the privatization rules and plan to join whichever consortium wins after the auction.
Valecom is one of two consortia planning to participate in the April 29 privatization auction.
The other is led by Brazilian steelmaker CSN and includes Nations Bank, Opportunity Asset Management, South Africa's Gencor and four Brazilian pension funds, Previ, Petros, Funcef and Funcesp.
The four pension funds already have a joint voting stake of around 10.03 percent in CVRD which would give the CSN consortium a controling position in CVRD if it wins the auction.
CSN is also holding talks with Brazilian pulp and paper group Suzano, construction firm Camargo Correia and U.S. aluminium company Alcoa.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
